title: Network Operations Primer
scenario: Welcome to Network Operations Primer. Before proceeding, you must master these essential networking terms. Network Management System (NMS): Platform for monitoring and managing network devices. Collects data via SNMP, NetFlow, syslog. Provides dashboards, alerts, trending. Examples: SolarWinds, PRTG, Nagios, Zabbix. Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP): Port 161 (polling) / 162 (traps). UDP. Monitors network devices. v1/v2c use cleartext community strings. v3 adds authentication and AES encryption (AuthPriv). MIB stores OIDs. Management Information Base (MIB): SNMP database structure. Hierarchical tree of OIDs (Object Identifiers) each representing a manageable object on a device (e.g., interface stats, CPU usage). Defined in RFC/vendor MIBs. Object Identifier (OID): Unique numeric path in the SNMP MIB tree identifying a specific managed object. Example: 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1 = sysDescr. SNMP manager polls OIDs to get device metrics.
question: What does NMS stand for?
explanation: NMS stands for Network Management System.
